landingHome.statWeeklyLabel: a week with Plus: less than a coffee
landingHome.proInfoFidelity: The loyalty card your customers never lose: they keep it on their phone, you stamp it with one tap and choose the reward. See who is one step away from the reward and invite them back: more visits, without printing a single card.
landingHome.proInfoMenu: Your venue’s menu with a QR code on the table, even in several languages: perfect for tourists. Change a dish or a price from your phone and the QR stays the same: no reprints, always up to date.
landingHome.proInfoQuotes: Quotes with your logo and letterhead in a few minutes, even from your phone. Save them, download them as PDF and send them by email or WhatsApp: you look professional right away.
landingHome.proInfoReceipts: Deliveries, loans, deposits and equipment handed over: the recipient confirms from their phone and you keep proof with date and time. No more lost papers or arguments about what was delivered.
landingHome.proInfoMagazzino: Products, stock, incoming and outgoing goods always under control. Scan barcodes with your phone, get alerts when a product is running low and export the data for your accountant.
landingHome.proInfoKordata: Become a supplier for Kordate, the KUMANI community’s group purchases: offer your products to groups of Kumani and, once the minimum number is reached, sell to many customers at once.
landingHome.proInfoQrPro: Dynamic QR codes you print only once: change the destination whenever you want (menu, daily offer, website) and see how many times they are scanned. Ideal for flyers, shop windows and business cards.
landingHome.proInfoFirmaEmail: A professional email signature with logo, contacts, social links and your Link in Bio, ready to paste into Gmail and Outlook. Every email you send becomes a business card.
landingHome.proInfoCalcolatrici: Everyday calculations for business owners: VAT to add or remove, withholding tax, discounts, markup and margin. Instant, clear results, no spreadsheets.
landingHome.proBannerText: Shops, restaurants, craftspeople, freelancers: with the Pro plan you get digital loyalty cards, a table-QR menu, quotes and receipts in a few taps, AI-made offers and a Professional Area with your business stats. You can also become a Kordata supplier and organise events for your customers.

whatsappPage.template1Message:
Hi! 👋 I wanted to tell you about KUMANI, an app I’m using that I think could be useful for you too.

It has lots of everyday tools: check whether an IBAN or a phone number is suspicious, follow the latest scams, relax with breathing exercises and mandalas to colour, play with friends and find a community of people who help each other.

You sign up for free in a minute, no card needed, and choose what to use.

Here’s the link: {url}
Let me know what you think! 😊
whatsappPage.template2Message:
Good morning,

I’d like to introduce KUMANI, an Italian platform that brings together practical tools for work and everyday life in a single account.

These include online scam checks (IBANs, phone numbers and, with the Plus plan, websites and emails), organising deadlines and documents and, for businesses, services such as a landing page, quotes, receipts and client management.

Signing up is free; the Plus (€59 a year) and Pro (€169 a year) plans add more services.

You can find all the details here: {url}
I’m happy to answer any questions.
Kind regards
whatsappPage.template3Message:
Hey! Let me tell you something 😊

I’ve been using KUMANI for a while and it’s making my life easier: before a bank transfer I check the IBAN, when a strange call comes in I see if others have reported it, and I’ve stopped forgetting deadlines.

[Write here in one line what you use it for]

It’s not one of those apps full of ads: they’re practical tools, and there’s a community of people who help each other.

If you want to try it, signing up is free: {url}
If you need a hand getting started, call me!
whatsappPage.template4Message:
Hi! It was a pleasure meeting you today 😊

As I mentioned, this is KUMANI, the app I use: tools against scams, for organising deadlines and documents, for businesses, and a community of people who help each other.

Here’s the link so you can have a look in your own time: {url}

If you like, next time we meet I’ll show you how I use it. Let me know what you think! ☕
whatsappPage.editHint: Your invite link always stays in the message: if you delete it, we add it at the end.
whatsappPage.template5Message:
Hi! 👋 Let me introduce KUMANI, the platform I use: with one account you get lots of practical tools for everyday life.

🛡️ It protects you from scams: check a website, an email, an IBAN or a phone number before you trust it.
📅 It keeps you organised: car and home deadlines, bills, diary and documents all in one place.

whatsappPage.template6Message:
Hi! With so many scams going around lately, I recommend KUMANI 🛡️

Free for everyone:
✅ check an IBAN before a bank transfer
✅ find out if a number that called you has been reported by others
✅ read the latest scams, reported by the community
✅ get the Anti-Scam Manual with real examples and what to do

With the Plus plan you can also check websites, suspicious emails and fake photos.

Signing up is free: {url}
Better to check for a minute than to regret it later!
whatsappPage.template7Title: For people with a thousand deadlines
whatsappPage.template7Desc: For anyone who forgets car tax, bills and appointments.
whatsappPage.template7Message:
Hi! Since you always have a thousand things to remember, I recommend KUMANI 📅

With the Plus plan everything is in one place:
🚗 car tax, insurance and MOT
🏠 bills, maintenance and utilities at home
📄 ID card, driving licence and expiring documents, with reminders
💶 monthly spending, so you get to the end of the month more relaxed
🗓️ a diary with appointments and notes

Plus costs €59 a year, less than €5 a month, and meanwhile you can sign up for free and try the free services.

Here’s the link: {url}
whatsappPage.template8Desc: For tradespeople, shops, restaurants and freelancers.
whatsappPage.template8Message:
Hi! Since you run a business, I want to tell you about KUMANI 💼

With the Pro plan you get the tools to be found and work better:
🌐 a landing page so people find you online
🧾 quotes and receipts ready to send to clients
👥 your client list with the jobs to do
🍽️ a digital menu with a QR code, for venues
🛍️ an online shop and a loyalty card

Pro costs €169 a year and you can try it free for 15 days.

Take a look here: {url}
If you like, I’ll show you how I use it.
whatsappPage.template9Desc: For people looking for company, help or opportunities nearby.
whatsappPage.template9Message:
Hi! Fancy meeting new people? 🤝

KUMANI has a community of people who help each other, and these things are free:
📌 the noticeboard to offer or look for something
🎉 events in your city
⏳ the time bank: help someone for an hour and get an hour back when you need it
🍕 Convivium, to organise an evening and invite friends with a link
🛒 Kordata, for group buying and saving money

Sign up for free here: {url}
See you inside!
whatsappPage.template10Desc: To protect the people most exposed to scams.
whatsappPage.template10Message:
Hi! I’m writing about something important 💛

Scammers target older people above all: fake couriers, fake grandchildren in trouble, “bank” texts that aren’t from the bank.

With KUMANI, for free, you can:
✅ check an IBAN before a bank transfer
✅ see if a number that called has been reported
✅ read the latest scams explained simply

It’s easy to use at any age. I recommend it for you and for your parents or grandparents: I’ll help you sign them up.

Here’s the link: {url}

acoustic.intro: A hearing screening test: for each ear you'll hear a series of tones that start very quiet and gradually become more audible. Press "I hear it" as soon as you perceive the sound.
acoustic.medicalDisclaimer: A self-assessment test, not a calibrated clinical audiometric exam. It does not replace the advice of a doctor or audiologist.
acoustic.deviceCheckBody: For a more accurate result we recommend using headphones, or turning on speakerphone at a moderate volume.
acoustic.deviceCheckMobileWarning: On smartphone you must wear headphones or turn on speakerphone before starting: the earpiece speaker is not suitable for this test.
acoustic.instructionsBody: The test takes about 2-3 minutes and covers both ears across 6 different frequencies, from low to high. For each sound, press "I hear it" as soon as you can perceive it, even faintly. If you press nothing, the test automatically moves to the next sound after a few seconds. Between sounds there is always a pause of silence of varying length: tap only when you really hear the sound.
acoustic.waitingLabel: Listen carefully: tap “I hear it” only when you hear the sound.
acoustic.earlyPress: No sound right now: wait until you hear it
acoustic.earlyPressWarning: You tapped “I hear it” {count} times with no sound: for a reliable result, take the test again calmly and tap only when you really hear the tone.
acoustic.autoAdvanceHint: If you don't hear anything, wait: it will automatically move to the next sound.
acoustic.resultsSummary: Sensitivity score: {score}/100 (higher means you perceived the tones at lower volumes).
acoustic.saveError: We couldn't save the result. Please try again.
acoustic.notLoggedIn: You need to be logged in.

aureya.acuityCardDescription: Say which way the letter “E” is facing as it gets smaller: no time limit, one eye at a time.

calibration.title: Measure your screen
calibration.body: Place a credit card, debit card or health card upright on the rectangle and make it bigger or smaller until it’s the same size. You only need to do this once: we remember it on this device.

acuity.title: Visual acuity
acuity.intro: The classic check with the letter “E”: say which way it faces as it gets smaller and smaller. Speed doesn’t matter: answer calmly.
acuity.medicalDisclaimer: A self-check, not an eye examination. The result depends on screen, light and distance and is only indicative. If you wear glasses or lenses for close-up vision, keep them on.
acuity.how1: Hold the screen about {distance} cm from your eyes, in a well-lit room.
acuity.how2: One eye at a time: cover the other with the palm of your hand, without pressing.
acuity.how3: For each “E”, tap the arrow for the direction its “legs” point. If you can’t see it, tap “I can’t see it”.
acuity.how4: The first time you measure the screen with a card: it’s needed to show the letter at the right size.
acuity.eyeBody: Cover {cover} with your palm and hold the screen about {distance} cm away.
acuity.question: Which way do the “legs” of the E point?
acuity.resultsAdvice: This is an indicative result. If you see worse than before, if one eye is very different from the other or you have doubts, see an optometrist or eye doctor.
acuity.saveError: The result couldn’t be saved. Try again.
acuity.how5: On a computer you can also answer with the arrow keys: handy when you’re far from the screen.
acuity.limitedNote: Your screen can’t show even smaller letters at this distance: your real result may be higher. To measure further, take the test again on a smartphone.

amsler.title: Amsler grid
amsler.intro: A simple check to notice whether the lines of a grid look wavy, blurred or missing. No time limit and no score.
amsler.medicalDisclaimer: A self-check, not an eye examination. If you wear reading glasses, keep them on. If you notice wavy lines or missing areas for the first time, contact an eye doctor without delay.
amsler.how1: Hold the screen about 30 cm from your eyes, in a well-lit room.
amsler.how2: One eye at a time: cover the other and keep looking at the black dot in the centre, without moving your gaze.
amsler.how3: Tap the squares where the lines look wavy, blurred, faded or missing. If everything looks normal, don’t tap anything.
amsler.eyeBody: Cover {cover} with your palm and hold the screen about 30 cm away.
amsler.gridHint: Look only at the dot in the centre. Tap the squares where the lines look wavy, blurred or missing; tap again to remove the mark.
amsler.markedCount: {count, plural, =0 {No squares marked} one {# square marked} other {# squares marked}}
amsler.zonesMarked: {count, plural, one {# area marked} other {# areas marked}}
amsler.adviceMarked: You marked some areas: if it’s the first time or things have changed, contact an eye doctor soon. Repeat the grid regularly to notice any changes.
amsler.adviceClear: No areas marked. Repeat the grid now and then: what matters most is noticing changes over time.
amsler.saveError: The result couldn’t be saved. Try again.

verifoto.riskExplain: The number sums up all the signs found (credentials, metadata, AI detector): the higher it is, the more likely the photo was generated or edited with artificial intelligence. It is not an exact percentage or proof: the AI detector below makes the result more reliable.
verifoto.title: VeriFoto
verifoto.heroText: Check whether an image was generated or edited with artificial intelligence: digital credentials, metadata, a retouch map and a specialised AI detector.
verifoto.uploadHint: JPG, PNG or WebP up to 15 MB. Basic checks run on your device: the photo is not uploaded.
verifoto.invalidFile: Unsupported file: use a JPG, PNG or WebP image up to 15 MB.
verifoto.elaHint: Areas much brighter than the rest may indicate pasted or retouched parts. Sharp edges and text always look brighter: that is normal. It is a visual aid, not proof.
verifoto.verdict_ai: Probably generated or edited with AI
verifoto.verdictText_ai: There are concrete signs that the image was created or edited with artificial intelligence. Do not rely on this photo as proof.
verifoto.verdictText_uncertain: The signs are not enough to tell. Use the AI detector below and the manual checks, and stay careful.
verifoto.verdictText_likely_real: No signs of artificial intelligence and several signs of a genuinely taken photo. No check is infallible, though.
verifoto.clueSourceTypeAi: The file declares it was created with artificial intelligence.
verifoto.clueSourceTypeComposite: The file declares that some parts were created or edited with artificial intelligence.
verifoto.clueC2paAi: Digital credential (Content Credentials) from {tool}: image created with AI.
verifoto.clueC2paOther: Digital credential (Content Credentials) present, created by: {tool}.
verifoto.clueC2paPresent: Digital credential (Content Credentials) present, with no mention of artificial intelligence.
verifoto.clueGeneratorAi: An artificial intelligence tool appears in the metadata: {tool}.
verifoto.clueGenerationParams: The file contains AI generation parameters (prompt, steps, model).
verifoto.clueEditor: The photo was processed with an editing program: {software}.
verifoto.clueCamera: Complete shooting data (date and settings) from the camera {camera}.
verifoto.clueNoCamera: No camera shooting data: normal for screenshots and photos shared on social media, but also for AI images.
verifoto.clueDetectorAi: The AI detector estimates a {pct}% chance that the image was generated or edited with AI.
verifoto.clueDetectorReal: The AI detector estimates only a {pct}% chance of artificial intelligence involvement.
verifoto.clueDetectorUnsure: The AI detector is not sure ({pct}%): intermediate result.
verifoto.detectorText: A specialised model from an external provider analyses the pixels and estimates whether the image was generated or edited with AI.
verifoto.detectorConsent: I agree that a reduced copy of the photo, without metadata, is sent to a specialised external service for analysis. KUMANI does not keep it.
verifoto.detectorLeft: {count, plural, =0 {No analyses left today} one {# analysis left today} other {# analyses left today}}
verifoto.detector_quota: The AI detector has reached this month’s free limit: it will be available again next month. On-device checks still work.
verifoto.detector_user_limit: You have used all of today’s detector analyses: try again tomorrow.
verifoto.detector_unavailable: The AI detector is not available right now. On-device checks still work.
verifoto.detector_error: The photo could not be analysed. Try again with another image.
verifoto.detector_not_allowed: The detector is reserved for subscribers with an active plan.
verifoto.manualText: Upload the same photo to Google Lens or TinEye: if it already exists elsewhere (perhaps different or older), it may be stolen or altered.
verifoto.disclaimer: VeriFoto provides clues, not certainties: no automatic check detects 100% of AI or retouched images, and compressed or filtered photos may give uncertain results. It is not an expert report.

verifoto.placeOpenMap: See the spot on the map

verifoto.placeAgeMonths: {n, plural, one {# month ago} other {# months ago}}

verifoto.placeTip: Compare it with what you were told: if the house “is in Rimini” but the photo was taken elsewhere, or the photo “from today” is years old, that is a warning sign. The photo data stays on your device; the map opens only if you tap it.
verifoto.synthidText: Images made with Gemini, ChatGPT and other AI tools from Google partners carry an invisible watermark in the pixels, which stays even if the photo is cropped or its data is removed. Google’s check is free: upload the same photo there.

svat.scamListPhishing: Listed in an international feed of active phishing sites: it imitates a bank, courier or well-known service to steal passwords and card details.

svat.scamListBafin_impersonation: Flagged by the German financial authority (BaFin) on {date}: fake bank or a site impersonating a real company. Do not send money or details.
svat.scamListIvass: Blocked or flagged by IVASS (Italy) on {date}: it sold insurance without authorisation. Policies from these sites are fake: do not pay.
svat.communityConfirmed: Reported as a scam by the community ({count}) and confirmed by the KUMANI Staff. Do not pay or share any details.
svat.paymentsRisky: The only payment options are bank transfer, top-ups or crypto: if the seller disappears, the money won’t come back. Only pay by card or PayPal.
svat.paymentsMoneyTransfer: Western Union or MoneyGram are among the payments: genuine shops don’t use them and money sent can’t be recovered.
svat.paymentsSafe: You can pay by card or PayPal: if something goes wrong you can ask for a refund.
svat.pricesExtreme: Huge discounts everywhere (up to {max}%): the typical shop window of fake stores.
svat.pricesClosingDown: “Closing down” sale with discounts up to {max}%: a trick fake shops use a lot. Check carefully before paying.
svat.placeholderText: The site still has dummy or sample text (e.g. “lorem ipsum”): built in a hurry and never finished.
svat.webRiskClean: Google does not flag it as a dangerous site.
svat.webRiskPhishing: Google flags it as a deceptive (phishing) site: it’s built to steal passwords, data and money. Don’t enter anything.
svat.webRiskMalware: Google flags it as a site that spreads viruses: don’t open it or download anything.
svat.webRiskUnwanted: Google flags it for pushing unwanted software: don’t download anything.
svat.officialIvassCompany: Official site of {name}, an insurance company supervised by IVASS (Italy).
svat.officialIvassIntermediary: Site declared to IVASS (Italy) by a registered insurance intermediary.
svat.ipLoggerDetected: {domain} is a spy link: whoever opens it gives its creator their IP address, approximate area and device. Do not open or forward it.
svat.ipLoggerAlertTitle: Warning: this is a spy link
svat.youngDomain: Young domain: registered {days} days ago. Many scam sites stay online only a few weeks or months: check carefully before paying or leaving data.
svat.reportSite: Report this site to the Anti-Scam Network
svat.reportSiteHint: The Staff checks it: if it is a scam, everyone who looks it up will be warned.
svat.scamPatternAlertTitle: Warning: it has the typical signs of a scam
svat.scamPatternRecoveryAuthority: It promises to recover or unlock funds and crypto and claims to be authorised or certified by CONSOB or the Bank of Italy, which do not authorise sites like this. It is the “fund recovery” scam: do not pay anything or leave your data.
svat.scamPatternRecovery: It promises to recover or unlock funds and crypto, with other risk signs (young domain or Telegram-only contacts). It is the “fund recovery” scam pattern: do not pay anything or leave your data.
svat.scamPatternAuthority: It claims to be authorised or certified by CONSOB, the Bank of Italy or IVASS, but it is a young site or built with an automatic builder. Authorities do not “certify” sites: check their official registers.
svat.scamPatternTopic: It talks about recovering or unlocking funds and crypto: the theme of the “fund recovery” scam. If they ask for money or data to recover what you lost, it is almost always a scam.
svat.scamPatternLoan: It promises loans even to people “blacklisted” or with bad credit, with subsidised rates “for everyone” or public grants, on a young site. It is the “easy loan” scam: sooner or later they ask for a fee or deposit and the loan never arrives. Never pay anything in advance.
svat.scamPatternPhishing: Fake login page: it asks for your user code and password while posing as {brand}, but the site is {domain} and does not belong to {brand} (the real site is {official}). This is phishing, meant to steal access to your account. Do not enter anything; if you already did, change your password right away and contact {brand}.
svat.redirectTo: The link does not stay on {from}: it takes you to {to}. The checks below are run on the destination site, where you would actually end up.
svat.scamPatternPhishingCard: Fake payment page: it asks for your card details while posing as {brand}, but the site is {domain} and does not belong to {brand} (the real site is {official}). This is phishing, meant to steal your card. Do not enter anything; if you already did, block your card right away by calling your bank.

aboutPage.metaDescription: Kumani doesn't sell dreams: it lends hands. Discover the story, the meaning of the name and the manifesto of Kumani, the community of professional tools for people who work for themselves.
aboutPage.title: Hands that lend you a hand.
aboutPage.subtitle: Not a company that sells dreams: a community that lends hands.
aboutPage.namePara1: KUMANI comes from two words. KU comes from the Japanese 組 (kumi): “group, gathering, people working side by side.” MANI is the oldest Italian word for work: the hands that build, help, create.
aboutPage.namePara2: KUMANI means “hands together”: because anyone working alone needs extra hands, and a community willing to lend them.
aboutPage.namePara3: At the heart of Kumani there have never been algorithms, compensation plans or promises. There are people.
aboutPage.story1Text: For years we lived alongside extraordinary people: salespeople, consultants, networkers, artisans of their own business. People with big hearts and an empty toolbox. Around them, a market selling dreams: promised cars, yachts in photographs, courses worth thousands of euros, and seven different paid apps to do what should be done in one place. Hands held out to promise. Never a hand held out to help.
aboutPage.story2Title: A lifetime of lending a hand
aboutPage.story2Text1: The founder of KUMANI has spent a lifetime lending a hand. Since the 1990s, when technology was starting to change everything, they have helped people and businesses solve all kinds of IT problems.
aboutPage.story2Text2: And every time it came down to the same discovery: people don't need promises, they need simple tools and someone who makes them easy to use. KUMANI is that same hand, multiplied: all the tools we have gathered, in one place, at the service of people who work.
aboutPage.story3Text: That's how KUMANI was born: not a company that sells dreams, but a community that lends hands. One place, every tool. An honest price: €59 a year for everyone with the Plus plan, €169 a year for professionals with the Pro plan. Public rules, real benefits, zero mirages. Because before being professionals, we're human. And humans, when they have the right hands, do extraordinary things on their own.
aboutPage.manifesto4Rest: €59 a year for the Plus plan, €169 a year for the Pro plan for professionals.
aboutPage.manifesto5Rest: that's why we also teach you to breathe.
aboutPage.manifesto6Rest: public rules, real benefits, no tricks.
aboutPage.closingTitle: Kumani. Hands that lend you a hand.
aboutPage.closingSubtitle: Public rules, real benefits, an honest price forever: €59 a year with Plus, €169 a year with Pro.
aboutPage.footerTagline: Hands that lend you a hand.

affinity.arch_faro_short: A steady point that lights the way.
affinity.arch_faro_desc: You are a steady point: consistent and reliable, the people close to you know they can count on you. You hold the course when others get lost and light the way without making noise.
affinity.arch_marea_short: Energy in motion that carries others along.
affinity.arch_marea_desc: Your energy never stands still: you know how to speed up when needed and carry others with you. With you things happen, and even the flattest days change rhythm.
affinity.arch_bosco_short: Depth and curiosity down every path.
affinity.arch_bosco_desc: You are depth and curiosity: every path intrigues you, you love understanding how things and people work. Behind each of your questions there is always a world to explore.
affinity.arch_brace_short: A warmth that makes people feel at home.
affinity.arch_brace_desc: You warm up everyone around you: welcoming and empathetic, people feel at home with you. You don't make much noise, but without you the evening wouldn't be the same.
affinity.arch_vento_short: Free, unpredictable, always on the move.
affinity.arch_vento_desc: Free and unpredictable: you love new things, changes of plan and roads never taken. You bring fresh air wherever you go and push others to dare a little more.

affinity.compat_mid: You complete each other: where one slows down, the other pushes.
affinity.compat_low: Opposites attract: together you see twice as much.

contactPage.faqSubtitle: Quick answers to the questions we receive most often.
contactPage.faq1Q: I can't log in to my account: what can I do?
contactPage.faq1A: Make sure you're using the same email you signed up with. If you can't remember your password, use "Forgotten your password?" on the login page: we'll send you a link to create a new one (check your spam folder too). If you still can't get in, write to us using the form above and choose "Support and assistance".
contactPage.faq2Q: How much do the Plus and Pro subscriptions cost?
contactPage.faq2A: The Plus subscription costs €59 a year, Pro €169 a year. Pro unlocks all the tools and advanced features, and you can try it free for 15 days before deciding.
contactPage.faq3Q: How do renewal and cancellation work?
contactPage.faq3A: The subscription lasts one year. Before it expires we'll remind you about renewal, so you can decide at your own pace. You can cancel whenever you like from the subscription section of your profile: you stay active until the end of the period you've already paid for.
contactPage.faq4Q: What are KU Karma and KU Points?
contactPage.faq4A: They're a way to reward your participation: you earn them by using KUMANI and contributing to the community. They can only be spent within the platform (rewards, perks, discounts) and they aren't money: they can't be converted into cash or transferred outside KUMANI.
contactPage.faq5Q: How do you handle my personal data?
contactPage.faq5A: We only use your data to make KUMANI work and we never sell it to anyone. You'll find all the details in the privacy policy. If you'd like to view, correct or delete your data, write to us choosing the topic "Privacy and personal data".
contactPage.faq6Q: How do I report a problem, abuse or inappropriate behaviour?
contactPage.faq6A: Many items have a "Report" button: it's the quickest way. Alternatively, write to us using the form and tell us what happened, with links or screenshots if you have them. Every report is read by the Staff and handled confidentially.
contactPage.faq7Q: Why do you ask me to verify my identity for Kordata and Events?
contactPage.faq7A: Kordata group purchases and KUMANI Events involve money and meeting in person: identity verification protects everyone from fake profiles and scams. The document is checked by the Staff and then deleted: we only keep the outcome.
contactPage.faq8Q: I'm a professional: can I work with KUMANI?
contactPage.faq8A: Of course! Whether you'd like to offer your services to the community or propose an agreement or partnership, write to us choosing "I'm a professional" or "Partnerships and collaborations": we'll get back to you to talk it through together.
contactPage.faqMore: Didn't find the answer you were looking for?

checkmail.title: KUMANI CheckMail
checkmail.heroText: Got a suspicious email? Upload or paste it: we check the sender, digital signatures, links, attachments and text, and tell you how risky it is. Scams give themselves away in the details: we read them all.
checkmail.fileHint: The most complete way: save the email as a file (.eml or .msg) and upload it here. That way we also read the hidden headers, which show who really sent it.
checkmail.howToFileTitle: How do I save the email as a file?
checkmail.howToGmail: Gmail (desktop): open the email → ⋮ menu at the top right → "Download message".
checkmail.howToOutlook: Outlook (app): open the email → File → "Save As", or drag it to the desktop.
checkmail.howToOutlookWeb: Outlook.com: open the email → ⋯ → "Download" → "Download as EML".
checkmail.howToThunderbird: Thunderbird: open the email → File → "Save As" → "File".
checkmail.pasteHint: Paste the full source of the email here (headers and text).
checkmail.howToPasteTitle: Where do I find the source?
checkmail.howToPasteGmail: Gmail (desktop): open the email → ⋮ menu → "Show original" → "Copy to clipboard".
checkmail.howToPasteOutlook: Outlook: open the email → ⋯ → "View" → "View message source", then copy everything.
checkmail.quickHint: On your phone? Copy the sender address, the subject and the text of the email.
checkmail.quickNote: Without the file or the source we cannot read the hidden headers, so the check is more limited. If you can, repeat it from a computer.
checkmail.privacyNote: The email is analyzed and not stored: we only keep how many checks you made today. The text may also be read by an artificial intelligence service, which does not use it to train its models.
checkmail.disclaimer: CheckMail provides clues, not certainties: no automatic check catches 100% of scams, and a "low" result does not guarantee the email is safe. When in doubt, do not click, do not reply, and contact the company through its official channels. The result is not an expert assessment.

checkmail.error_empty: Upload a file or write the content of the email.
checkmail.error_too_large: The email is too large (max 4 MB).

checkmail.error_error: Something went wrong. Please try again shortly.
checkmail.level_high: High risk: almost certainly a scam
checkmail.levelText_high: We found strong signs of a scam. Do not click the links, do not open attachments and do not reply.
checkmail.levelText_medium: There are suspicious signs. Before doing anything, check with the company through its official channels.
checkmail.levelText_low: We found no major signs of a scam. Stay careful anyway: no check is 100% certain.
checkmail.noSignals: No risk signals in the technical checks.
checkmail.aiUnavailable: AI text reading is not available right now: the result is based on the technical checks only.
checkmail.advice_high: Do not click, do not open attachments and do not reply. If you already entered passwords or card details, change the password now and call your bank using the number on the back of your card. Then report the email as spam or phishing and delete it.
checkmail.advice_medium: Do not use the links in the email: open the official website yourself by typing the address, or call the company on a number you know. Never send passwords, codes or card details by email.
checkmail.advice_low: It looks like a normal email, but stay alert: if it asks for money, passwords or codes, always check through official channels before acting.
checkmail.f_auth_dmarc_fail: Your email provider reports that the sender is NOT authentic (DMARC failed).
checkmail.f_auth_spf_dkim_fail: The server that sent the email is not authorized by the sender's domain (SPF/DKIM failed).
checkmail.f_auth_dkim_fail: The sender's digital signature is invalid (DKIM failed for {domain}): the email may be forged.
checkmail.f_auth_ok: Sender authentication passed (SPF {spf}, DKIM {dkim}, DMARC {dmarc}): it confirms the sending domain, not that the email is trustworthy.
checkmail.f_no_headers: Without the technical headers the check is partial: upload the file or paste the source for a full check.
checkmail.f_forwarded: This is a forwarded email: I check the original sender ({sender}), not the person who forwarded it.
checkmail.f_forwarded_unknown: This is a forwarded email but I can't find the original sender: for a full check, also paste the original message's «From:» line.
checkmail.f_sender_missing: The sender has no email address: genuine messages always have one.
checkmail.f_brand_from_freemail: It claims to be {brand} but writes from a free email address ({domain}).
checkmail.f_brand_domain_mismatch: It claims to be {brand} but the sender's domain ({domain}) is not an official one.
checkmail.f_idn_sender: The sender's domain uses special characters that can imitate normal letters ({domain}).
checkmail.f_display_name_address: The displayed name contains an address ({shown}) different from the real one ({real}).
checkmail.f_reply_to_mismatch: Replies would go to another domain ({replyTo}) instead of {from}.
checkmail.f_link_text_mismatch: A link shows one address but leads elsewhere ({example}).
checkmail.f_link_ip: A link leads to a numeric (IP) address instead of a named website.
checkmail.f_link_shortener: A link is shortened ({domain}) and hides the real destination.
checkmail.f_link_risky_tld: A link leads to a domain with an extension often used in scams ({domain}).
checkmail.f_lookalike_link: A link leads to a domain that imitates {brand} ({domain}).
checkmail.f_idn_link: A link uses special characters that can imitate a well-known site.
checkmail.f_brand_links_offsite: It asks for your data on behalf of {brand} but the links lead outside the official sites ({domain}).
checkmail.f_attachment_dangerous: Dangerous attachment ({name}): do not open it.
checkmail.f_attachment_html: Web page attachment ({name}): often a fake login form.
checkmail.f_attachment_archive: Compressed attachment ({name}): it may hide dangerous files.
checkmail.f_content_account_threat: It threatens to block or suspend an account ("{phrase}").
checkmail.f_content_credentials: It asks you to enter or confirm personal or login data ("{phrase}").
checkmail.f_content_payment_pressure: It asks for unusual payments or new bank details ("{phrase}").
checkmail.f_content_parcel: It talks about a parcel to release or shipping fees ("{phrase}").
checkmail.f_content_investment: It talks about investments, trading or returns ("{phrase}"): typical of financial scams.
checkmail.f_generic_greeting: Generic greeting ("Dear customer"): people who know you use your name.
checkmail.f_template_placeholder: It contains a forgotten template placeholder ("{text}"): a mass-produced email.
checkmail.f_pressure_foreign_link: It puts you under pressure but the link leads to a site unrelated to the sender ({domain}).
checkmail.f_mixed_script: The text mixes letters from different alphabets to fool spam filters (e.g. "{example}").
checkmail.f_domain_very_new: The domain {domain} was registered only {days} days ago.
checkmail.f_sender_no_mx: The sender's domain ({domain}) cannot receive email: a fake or disposable address.
checkmail.f_ai_high: Reading the text indicates a high probability of a scam.
checkmail.f_ai_medium: Reading the text finds suspicious elements.
checkmail.f_google_flagged: Google flags the link to {domain} as a dangerous site (phishing or viruses).
checkmail.f_scam_list: {domain} is on a list of scam sites (authorities or phishing).
checkmail.f_link_ip_logger: It contains a spy link ({domain}): if you open it, the sender sees your IP address, your area and your device. Do not open it.
checkmail.f_phishing_page: Fake login page: it asks for your user code and password while posing as {brand}, but the site is {domain} and does not belong to {brand} (the real site is {official}). This is phishing, meant to steal access to your account. Do not enter anything; if you already did, change your password right away and contact {brand}.
checkmail.f_phishing_page_card: Fake payment page: it asks for your card details while posing as {brand}, but the site is {domain} and does not belong to {brand} (the real site is {official}). This is phishing, meant to steal your card. Do not enter anything; if you already did, block your card right away by calling your bank.
checkmail.f_link_redirects: A link goes to another site: from {from} it lands on {to}. That is where you would actually end up.
checkmail.aiSkipped_clearScam: Reading the text wasn't needed: the technical checks already found serious signs of a scam.
checkmail.aiSkipped_clearSafe: Reading the text wasn't needed: the sender is verified (SPF/DKIM signatures) and there are no suspicious signs.

oxygen.title: OXYGEN
oxygen.heroText: A simple guide to 4-7-8 breathing: breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 7, breathe out for 8. The circle breathes with you and guides you step by step.
oxygen.chooseMode: How do you want to breathe today?
oxygen.modeGuidedHint: About 3 minutes: we guide you from start to finish, with a few words along the way.
oxygen.modeBreathHint: Go straight to the cycles: the circle and the count, no introduction.
oxygen.eyesNote: With sound or vibration on you can close your eyes: they tell you when to change phase (three different tones: in, hold, out).
oxygen.safety1: Sit or lie down somewhere quiet. Never while driving or doing anything that needs your attention.
oxygen.safety2: If it is your first time, do no more than 4 cycles: your body gets used to it gradually.
oxygen.safety3: If you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, stop and go back to breathing normally.
oxygen.safety4: If holding for 7 seconds is too much, slow down as feels comfortable: the rhythm matters, not perfection.
oxygen.safety5: It does not replace a doctor. If you have breathing or heart problems, or are pregnant, ask your doctor first.
oxygen.doneText: You completed {cycles} cycles of 4-7-8 breathing. Take this calm with you.
oxygen.phaseHint_inhale: Breathe in through your nose, slowly.
oxygen.phaseHint_exhale: Breathe out through your mouth, gently, all the way.
oxygen.prepareText: Empty your lungs completely with a long breath out through your mouth.
oxygen.intro1: Get comfortable. Back straight, shoulders soft, hands resting.
oxygen.intro2: These minutes are just for you. You do not have to do anything special: just breathe.
oxygen.intro3: For a moment, notice your breath as it is. Air comes in, air goes out. Change nothing.
oxygen.intro4: 4-7-8 breathing slows your rhythm and helps body and mind calm down.
oxygen.intro5: You will breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds, hold for 7 and breathe out through your mouth for 8. The circle will guide you.
oxygen.cycleTip2: With each breath out, let go of a little tension: shoulders, jaw, forehead.
oxygen.cycleTip3: If your mind wanders, that is fine: gently bring your attention back to the breath.
oxygen.cycleTipLast: Last cycle. Take all the time you need.
oxygen.outro1: Now let your breath return to its natural rhythm.
oxygen.outro2: Notice how you feel now: your body, your thoughts, your heartbeat.
oxygen.outro3: When your breath slows down, your body gets a simple message: you are safe.
oxygen.outro4: Come back whenever you like: before sleep, before an important moment, or when anxiety rises.
oxygen.disclaimer: OXYGEN is a relaxation exercise, not a medical device: it does not replace a doctor's advice or any treatment. Stop the exercise if you feel unwell.

documentoSicuro.badge: Security · Everything stays on your phone
documentoSicuro.heroText: Before sending a photo of your ID card or driving licence, add a note with the purpose and date, cover the details that aren't needed and remove the hidden information. That way, if the photo ends up in the wrong hands, it can't be reused.
documentoSicuro.privacyText: It is processed only here, in your browser: we don't upload it anywhere and we don't save it.
documentoSicuro.pickTitle: Choose the photo of your document
documentoSicuro.pickText: You can pick it from your gallery or take it right now with your phone.
documentoSicuro.errorDecode: I can't open this photo. Try another image, for example a JPG.
documentoSicuro.metaGps: This photo contains the GPS location of where it was taken.
documentoSicuro.metaGpsCoords: Coordinates: {lat}, {lon}. Whoever receives the original could work out where you live.
documentoSicuro.metaNone: We didn't find hidden data such as the location or the phone model.
documentoSicuro.metaRemoved: The hidden data is gone from the copy you download.
documentoSicuro.hideHint: Cover with a black box anything you weren't asked for: document number, signature, photo.
documentoSicuro.hideModeActive: Drag your finger or mouse across the photo to draw a black box.
documentoSicuro.previewAlt: Preview of the protected document, {count, plural, =0 {no areas covered} one {one area covered} other {# areas covered}}
documentoSicuro.hiddenCount: {count, plural, =0 {No areas covered} one {One area covered} other {# areas covered}}

documentoSicuro.presetsLabel: What are you sending it for?
documentoSicuro.purposeLabel: Who you're sending it to and why

documentoSicuro.watermarkDefaultNoPurpose: Copy dated {date}, not valid for other uses

documentoSicuro.tip1: Send only what you were asked for: often the front side or a few details are enough.
documentoSicuro.tip2: Never send strangers a selfie holding your document: that's exactly what scammers need to pretend to be you.
documentoSicuro.tip3: Use a different note for each person: if the copy gets passed around, you'll know where it came from.
documentoSicuro.tip4: Be wary of anyone who rushes you for your document over the phone, even if they say they're your bank.

verificaIban.heroTitle: Check the IBAN before you pay
verificaIban.heroText: Paste the IBAN you were given: we’ll tell you if it’s written correctly, which country it’s from and which warning signs to look out for, based on what you’re paying for.
verificaIban.privacy: The check happens entirely on your device: the IBAN is never sent or saved anywhere.
verificaIban.inputHint: You can paste it with or without spaces, in upper or lower case: we’ll tidy it up.
verificaIban.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy: please select it and copy it by hand
verificaIban.issueEmpty: You haven’t typed anything yet: paste the IBAN in the box above.
verificaIban.issueInvalidChars: There are characters that can’t appear in an IBAN: {chars}. Only numbers and letters without accents are allowed.
verificaIban.issueBadCountryFormat: An IBAN always starts with two letters for the country (for example GB for the United Kingdom).
verificaIban.issueUnknownCountry: The first two letters ({country}) don’t match any country that uses IBANs. Check that you copied them correctly.
verificaIban.issueBadCheckDigits: After the two country letters there must be two numbers (the check digits). Be careful not to mix up the letter O and zero.
verificaIban.issueTooShort: {n, plural, one {# character is missing} other {# characters are missing}}: an IBAN from this country has {expected}. Maybe some got lost when copying.
verificaIban.issueTooLong: {n, plural, one {There is # character too many} other {There are # characters too many}}: an IBAN from this country has {expected}.
verificaIban.issueItalian_cin: The fifth character (the CIN) of an Italian IBAN must be a letter.
verificaIban.issueItalian_abi: The ABI code (the 5 characters after the CIN) must contain only numbers.
verificaIban.issueItalian_cab: The CAB code (the 5 characters after the ABI) must contain only numbers.
verificaIban.issueItalian_account: The account number (the last 12 characters) contains invalid characters.
verificaIban.issueChecksum: The check digits don’t add up: there is probably a typo, such as two swapped numbers or a wrong number. Double-check the IBAN with whoever gave it to you.
verificaIban.part_cin_help: A letter that checks the other parts.
verificaIban.part_abi_help: The code that identifies the bank.
verificaIban.part_account_help: The recipient’s account at that bank.
verificaIban.abiNote: The ABI code identifies the bank: you can check it on your bank’s website or on the Banca d’Italia website, which publishes the list of banks. If the bank isn’t the one you expect, stop and ask for an explanation.
verificaIban.contextHint: Choose the closest answer: we’ll show you the signs to watch out for.
verificaIban.ctxPrivateSeller: A private seller in my country (Marketplace, Vinted…)
verificaIban.ctxHolidayRental: A holiday home or a rental
verificaIban.ctxBill: A bill or a public body (taxes, fines, services)
verificaIban.ctxFamilyFriend: A relative or friend asking me for money
verificaIban.homeCountryHint: Only used to tell whether the IBAN is from another country. It isn’t saved.
verificaIban.signal_privateSellerForeign: The IBAN is from another country ({ibanCountry}), but the seller says they are a private person in your country. It isn’t necessarily a scam, but it’s a common sign in fake listings: ask for an explanation and, if you can, pay in person on delivery.
verificaIban.signal_privateSellerTip: Always stay in the platform’s chat and payment system. Be wary of anyone asking for an advance by bank transfer or top-up, or in a hurry to close the deal.
verificaIban.signal_holidayRentalForeign: The IBAN is from another country ({ibanCountry}). If the property is in your country, don’t ignore this sign: in fake listings the “owner” often lives abroad and asks for a deposit by bank transfer.
verificaIban.signal_holidayRentalTip: Only pay through the booking platform. Check the address on a map and the photos with a reverse image search. A reasonable deposit is around 20%: be wary of anyone asking for 50% or more before you’ve seen the place.
verificaIban.signal_onlineShopForeign: The IBAN is from another country ({ibanCountry}). Many genuine shops sell from abroad, but check that the website shows a company name, VAT number and address.
verificaIban.signal_onlineShopTip: A shop that only accepts bank transfers or crypto is a red flag. Prefer protected payments (credit card, PayPal “goods and services”) and look for reviews on independent websites.
verificaIban.signal_investmentStrong: Stop before you pay. Fake investments are among the scams that cost people the most: guaranteed or very high returns, celebrities “recommending” them, pressure to hurry and transfers to unknown accounts are typical signs.
verificaIban.signal_investmentCheck: Before sending any money, check that the firm is authorised on the websites of Consob and Banca d’Italia (and, if you live elsewhere, your own country’s financial regulator), and look at Consob’s list of blocked websites. Never install remote access apps such as AnyDesk.
verificaIban.signal_billCheck: Check the IBAN on the organisation’s official website or on the bill itself, never from a message, text or email. In Italy, taxes and fines are usually paid through pagoPA.
verificaIban.signal_billChanged: If you were told about a “new IBAN” by email, confirm the change by calling the number you already have, not the one in the message.
verificaIban.signal_familyCall: Call the number you know before paying. If a relative or friend writes from a new number or is in a big hurry, call them back on their usual number.
verificaIban.signal_familyPassword: Ask a question only they could answer, or use a family password: these days even voices can be cloned.
verificaIban.signal_otherTip: If the IBAN reached you by message, email or chat, check it through another channel: a call to a number you know or the official website. Hurry, secrecy and unusual payment methods are always warning signs.
verificaIban.keySentence: A valid IBAN doesn’t guarantee that the recipient is honest: it only tells you the code is written correctly.
verificaIban.tipInstant: An instant transfer can’t be undone: the money arrives within seconds.
verificaIban.tipProtected: When you can, prefer protected payments, such as a credit card or PayPal “goods and services”, which let you open a dispute.
verificaIban.tipPayee: Look at the recipient name your bank shows you: since October 2025, European banks compare the name with the IBAN (Verification of Payee). If you’re told the name doesn’t match, stop.
verificaIban.antitruffaLinkText: The most common scams, with real examples and what to do right away.
verificaIban.checkmailLinkText: Did you get the IBAN in a suspicious email? Check it here.
verificaIban.dossierAdvice: A correctly written IBAN doesn’t guarantee the recipient is honest: an instant transfer can’t be undone.
verificaIban.bankLoading: Looking up the bank in the Bank of Italy register…
verificaIban.bankKind_ip: Payment institution: usually an online account
verificaIban.bankKind_imel: Electronic money institution: usually an online account or a prepaid card
verificaIban.bankKind_poste: Poste Italiane BancoPosta or Postepay account
verificaIban.bankNotFound: ABI code not found in the Bank of Italy register: ask for an explanation before paying.
verificaIban.branchNotFound: Branch not found in the register (it may be an online account or a closed branch).
verificaIban.bankSource: Source: Bank of Italy public register of intermediaries, updated 21 October 2026. To find the bank and branch we only use the ABI and CAB codes.
verificaIban.onlineBankText: It is an account that can be opened in minutes from an app: many people use it normally, but it is also widely used in scams. If whoever asks for the payment says they are an Italian company or shop, ask for an explanation before paying.

scudoDati.heroTitle: Is your data already out there?
scudoDati.heroText: Find out if your email has appeared in a data breach, which data was exposed and what to do right away. You can also check whether a password has already leaked.
scudoDati.sources: Sources: XposedOrNot and Have I Been Pwned – Pwned Passwords. Results may be incomplete: a breach that hasn’t been published yet won’t show up. The email and the partial fingerprint of the password are sent to these services only for the check; we don’t store emails or passwords.
scudoDati.ownText: We check your account email against known data breaches.
scudoDati.safeText: This email doesn’t appear in known data breaches. Keep using a different password for each site and two-step sign-in.
scudoDati.breachedTitle: {count, plural, one {Found in 1 data breach} other {Found in # data breaches}}
scudoDati.breachedTextOwn: The data below was stolen from these sites and is circulating online. It doesn’t mean your account was hacked, but now is the time to secure it.
scudoDati.breachedTextOther: This email appears in known data breaches: let its owner know.
scudoDati.pasteNote: {count, plural, one {It also appears in 1 text published online (paste).} other {It also appears in # texts published online (pastes).}}
scudoDati.riskPlaintext: In this breach passwords were stored in plain text.
scudoDati.riskEasy: In this breach passwords were easy to crack.
scudoDati.tipPassword: Change your password on these sites and anywhere you reused it.
scudoDati.tip2fa: Turn on two-step sign-in (2FA) for email, bank and social media.
scudoDati.tipPhishing: Be wary of emails and texts that mention this breach or ask you to “verify your account”: they are often scams.
scudoDati.tipManager: Use a password manager to have a different, strong password for every site.
scudoDati.checkmailLink: Got a suspicious email? Check it with CheckMail
scudoDati.otherText: Check the email of a family member or your business. KU Karma is deducted only if the check succeeds.
scudoDati.err_auth: Please sign in again to run the check.
scudoDati.err_not_allowed: This service isn’t available for your account.
scudoDati.err_no_email: There is no email linked to your account.
scudoDati.err_limit: You’ve reached today’s checks. Try again tomorrow.
scudoDati.err_busy: The service is very busy right now. Please try again later.
scudoDati.err_failed: The check didn’t work. Try again shortly: nothing was deducted.
scudoDati.err_karma: You need {cost} KU Karma for this check.
scudoDati.pwText: Find out if a password has already appeared in a data breach. If so, stop using it.
scudoDati.pwNote: Your password never leaves your device and isn’t stored: only the start (5 characters) of its fingerprint is sent. The field is cleared after the check.
scudoDati.pwFound: {count, plural, one {Found 1 time: don’t use it} other {Found {formatted} times: don’t use it}}
scudoDati.pwFoundText: This password is on the lists scammers use to break into accounts. Change it wherever you use it.
scudoDati.pwNotFoundText: This password doesn’t appear in known data breaches. Still, use it on one site only.
scudoDati.pwError: The check didn’t work. Check your connection and try again.
scudoDati.googleIntro: Your phone number, home address and email found on Google are a gift to scammers and spammers. Google has a free tool, “Results about you”, to find out where they appear and ask for them to be removed from Search.
scudoDati.google_step1_text: Use the button above, or in the Google app tap your profile picture → “Results about you”. You need to be signed in to your Google account.
scudoDati.google_step2_title: Enter the details to look for
scudoDati.google_step2_text: Add the name, phone number, address and email you want to monitor and turn on alerts: Google will tell you when new results with your details appear.
scudoDati.google_step3_text: In the results to review you’ll see the pages where your contact details appear. Open them to see which site they’re on.
scudoDati.google_step4_text: For each result tap “Request to remove” and follow the steps. You can follow the status of your requests on the same page.
scudoDati.google_step5_text: While searching on Google, next to a result tap “⋮” → “Remove result” → “It shows my personal info” and complete the request.
scudoDati.googleLimitsTitle: What Google removes and what it doesn’t
scudoDati.googleLimitsText: Google removes the result from Search, not the page from the website: anyone who knows the page address can still see it. It usually accepts phone numbers, addresses, emails and ID numbers (passport, driving licence, ID card), but it doesn’t remove news articles or public-interest pages of public bodies.
scudoDati.googleMinorsText: For a minor’s information there is a dedicated form:
scudoDati.googleSourceTitle: To remove it for good: write to the website
scudoDati.googleSourceText: The surest way is to ask the website to delete your data: in Europe it’s your right (Article 17 GDPR, right to erasure). Copy the template, fill it in and send it to the site’s privacy address or contacts.
scudoDati.googleEmailTemplate:
Subject: Request to erase my personal data (Article 17 GDPR)

Dear Sir or Madam,
your website, on the page [page address], shows my personal data: [name, phone, address, email…].
Under Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) I request the erasure of this data without undue delay and in any case within one month, with written confirmation that it has been erased.

Full name: [ ]
Email for your reply: [ ]

Thank you,
[signature]
scudoDati.googleTips: Repeat the check now and then, turn on two-step verification on your accounts and be wary of messages that use your details to look credible: you can check a suspicious email with
scudoDati.googleNote: Google’s procedure and button names may change slightly over time. The official instructions are here:
scudoDati.photosTitle: Find out where your photos are used
scudoDati.photosIntro: The photos you post can end up on fake profiles, romance scams or sites you don’t know. With two free tools you can search the web for your photos: upload one of your images and see where it appears.
scudoDati.photos_step1_text: Start with your social media profile pictures, your most shared photos and those with your children. Only search for your own photos or those of people who asked you to.
scudoDati.photos_step2_text: Open Google Lens, upload the photo (or capture it from the screen) and scroll through “Exact matches” and similar images: you’ll see the sites where it appears.
scudoDati.photos_step3_text: TinEye finds the same image even when cropped or edited and shows where it appeared first. Using both finds more results.
scudoDati.photosFakeTitle: If your photo is on a fake profile
scudoDati.photosFakeText: Take screenshots of the profile and the page address, report it to the platform with the “Pretending to be me / impersonation” option and warn your contacts. If it’s used to scam or blackmail, report it to the police (cybercrime unit).
scudoDati.photosTipsBefore: Before posting, remove hidden data such as location from your photos with
scudoDati.photosTipsMiddle: ; if you receive a photo and want to know whether it’s real or AI-generated, check it with
scudoDati.photosNote: Google Lens and TinEye are free external services: you upload the photo to their site yourself. KUMANI does not receive or analyse your photos.
scudoDati.seeTitle: What a website sees about you
scudoDati.seeIntro: When you open a link, the website on the other side sees some information about you. It is what the "spy links" sent by strangers collect. See what they would see.
scudoDati.seeExplain: The area comes from your provider’s network: it usually shows your city or a nearby one, not your home address. Blackmailers who say "I know where you live" often have only this. To give it to no one: don’t open links from strangers and check them first with KUMANI.
scudoDati.seePrivacy: Only you can see this data: KUMANI does not save it.

calcolatrici.whInpsHelp: INPS separate scheme (gestione separata): the 4% surcharge is added to the fee and is part of the withholding tax base.
calcolatrici.whCassaHelp: Calculated on the fee. The supplementary contribution is not subject to withholding tax, but it is subject to VAT.
calcolatrici.whForfettarioHelp: No VAT, for example under the Italian flat-rate scheme (regime forfettario). Flat-rate taxpayers are usually not subject to withholding tax: in that case set the withholding rate to 0%.

calcolatrici.dsCascadeHelp: Discounts applied one after another, each on the already discounted price.
calcolatrici.dsCascadeExample: Example: 20% + 10% is not 30%, but a single equivalent discount of 28%.
calcolatrici.mgExplain: Markup is calculated on cost, margin on the selling price: if you buy at €60 and sell at €100, you earn €40, which is a 66.67% markup and a 40% margin.

registrazione.title: How to sign up
registrazione.summary: Create your KUMANI account in a few minutes and activate it with the code you receive by email.
registrazione.step1Text: On the homepage, tap the gold “Get Started” button at the top right. If someone sent you their invite link, open it: their code is filled in automatically.
registrazione.step2Text: Enter your first name, last name, email and a password of at least 8 characters, then choose your country and your city.
registrazione.step2Tip: Use an email you check often: that’s where the code to activate your account arrives.
registrazione.step3Text: If a Kumano invited you, enter their invite code. If you received a KUMANI voucher, enter it in the “Enter a voucher” field: your subscription is activated right away. Then tap “Create your account”.
registrazione.step4Text: We send you a code by email. Enter it in the “Verification code” field and tap “Verify and activate account”. Done: you’re in!
registrazione.step4Tip: Can’t find the email? Check your spam folder or tap “Resend code”.

accesso.title: How to log in
accesso.summary: Get into your account and recover your password if you’ve forgotten it.
accesso.step1Text: On the homepage, tap “Log in”, enter the email and password you chose when you signed up and tap “Log in”.
accesso.step2Text: Tap “Forgot password?” below the login button.
accesso.step3Text: Enter your email and tap “Reset Password”: we send you a code to choose a new one. Then log in with the new password.
accesso.step3Tip: You can add KUMANI to your phone’s Home screen: it opens like an app.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.summary: What you’ll find in the dashboard and how to reach the services you use most.
dashboard.step1Text: At the top you can change the language, open your profile and the Wallet, and log out. The star takes you to your favorite services.
dashboard.step2Text: The “Free” tier holds the services included for every member, with no time limit. Tap “Open” to use them and the little star to add them to your favorites.
dashboard.step3Text: Services are split into three tiers: Free, Plus and Pro. A Plus or Pro subscription unlocks every service in that tier; with a Pass you can also activate a single service.
dashboard.step4Text: Further down you’ll see the KU Karma you collect every day by logging in, your subscription status (with “Subscribe now” or “Activate via Voucher”) and your personal invite code.
dashboard.step5Title: The Community and the other pages
dashboard.step5Text: At the bottom you’ll find your KUMANI Community and quick links to the other pages: Community, Wallet and Noticeboard.

invito.title: Inviting with your link
invito.summary: Share your invite code or link and follow the people who become your Kumani.
invito.step1Text: Your personal invite code is in the dashboard. Tap the icon next to it to copy it: whoever signs up with your link becomes one of your Kumani.
invito.step2Text: On the Community page your link is ready: copy it, tap “Invite on WhatsApp” or “Share…” to send it with Instagram, Telegram and the other apps on your phone.
invito.step2Tip: A personal message works better than one sent to everyone: tell them why KUMANI is useful to you.
invito.step3Text: KUMI the octopus shows the 5 people you invited directly, one per tentacle, and how many active people there are under each of them. Anyone who signed up but hasn’t activated a subscription yet appears under “Not yet KUMANI”.
invito.step4Text: The rules are in the Wallet: you receive KU Points when someone you invited activates a subscription by paying with a card or upgrades to Pro.

voucher.title: Creating and using vouchers
voucher.summary: Vouchers come as rewards with qualifications: give them to new people and activate a voucher you received.
voucher.step1Text: With the Plus or Pro activations of the people you invited and your KU Points you become Kuman Green, Star or Black: the reward vouchers appear automatically in your Wallet, in the vouchers section.
voucher.step2Text: Copy the code or send it on WhatsApp: whoever receives it enters it when signing up and gets a year of KUMANI Plus. Vouchers are given away, not sold.
voucher.step3Text: Enter the code in the “Received a voucher?” field and tap “Redeem”: your subscription is activated right away. You can also enter it when you sign up.

wallet.title: Using the Wallet
wallet.summary: Your card, points, donations, badges and receipts: here’s what you’ll find in the Wallet.
wallet.step1Text: At the top is your KUMANI card with member number, active plan and expiry date. You can save the QR code with “Download QR”.
wallet.step2Text: Here you see your KU Karma, earned every day by logging in and using the tools, and your KU Points, received when someone you invited activates a subscription. Points are not money and can only be used inside the platform.
wallet.step3Text: In the Donations section you can donate your KU Points to the association KUMANI supports: every 10 KU Points donated = €1, which KUMANI pays to the association.
wallet.step4Text: The Kuman Green, Kuman Star and Kuman Black qualifications are reached with the activations of the people you invited and your KU Points, and come with reward vouchers. The bar shows how close you are to the next one.
wallet.step5Text: Further down you’ll find Digital Receipts (Pro plan), the coupons you got in the Ecosystem and the subscription renewal discount you can get with KU Karma.

qr_generator.title: Custom QR Code
qr_generator.summary: Create the QR code of your invite link, choose the colours and download it to print or share.
qr_generator.step1Text: The QR leads to your personal invite link. The “Target Link” is locked, so whoever scans it always becomes one of your Kumani.
qr_generator.step2Text: Change the “QR Code Color” and the “Background Color”, or tap one of the “Quick Themes”.
qr_generator.step2Tip: Keep good contrast between QR and background: a QR that is too light is hard to read.
qr_generator.step3Text: Check the preview and tap “Download PNG”: the image is high resolution, good for printing too.
qr_generator.step4Text: Print it on business cards and flyers, share it on social media or add it to your email signature.

whatsapp_messages.title: WhatsApp Messages
whatsapp_messages.summary: Ready-made messages with your invite link: choose the right tone and send it in seconds.
whatsapp_messages.step1Text: There are 10 messages: general ones (in a nutshell, friendly, personal, formal, after a meeting) and by topic (scams, deadlines, business, community, family). Tap «Open» on the right one: your invite link is already in the text.
whatsapp_messages.step2Text: Tap “Send on WhatsApp” to open WhatsApp with the message ready and choose who to send it to. Or tap “Copy message” and paste it wherever you like, even in another app.
whatsapp_messages.step2Tip: In WhatsApp you can edit the text before sending it: add the person’s name.
whatsapp_messages.step3Text: Always personalise the message, don’t send it to too many people at once and follow up with a call or a voice message.

link_in_bio.title: Link in Bio
link_in_bio.summary: Create your personal page with your links, to put in your Instagram, TikTok and other social bios.
link_in_bio.step1Text: In the “Bio Text” field write a sentence about yourself: it appears below your name.
link_in_bio.step2Text: Choose the page colour. You can preview the special themes (Northern lights, Moon over the lake, Savannah sunset) by tapping them: KU Karma are only used if you decide to unlock them.
link_in_bio.step3Text: Tap “Add Link” to add your links (website, social, shop…): your KUMANI invite link is always there. Then tap “Save Page”.
link_in_bio.step3Tip: Further down you can preview how the page will look.
link_in_bio.step4Text: Copy the page link and put it in your social bios, or tap “Visit your Link in Bio” to see it. Remember to save before sharing.

spotlight.title: Kumano of the Day
spotlight.summary: Tell your story and join the community showcase: every day one Kumano is featured. Reserved for active subscribers.
spotlight.step1Text: Fill in your name or nickname (never your surname), city, country, job or passion and a short story that can be read in 20 seconds.
spotlight.step2Text: Tap the KUMANI tools you use most: they appear together with your story.
spotlight.step3Text: Tick the consent to be shown to the community (the one for the homepage is optional) and tap “Save and join the showcase”. The KUMANI Staff approves the story, then it enters the Kumano of the Day rotation.
spotlight.step3Tip: You can remove your story from the showcase or the homepage whenever you like, from this same page.

events.title: KUMANI Events
events.summary: Find community meetups, workshops and evenings, sign up with one tap and get in with your pass.
events.step1Text: Search by city, country, language and date, or tap “Online only” for online events.
events.step2Title: Sign up and get your pass
events.step2Text: Open the event and tap “Join”: you get your pass with QR right away, and you’ll find it in “My passes”. Show it at the entrance: the organiser scans it and you’re in.
events.step2Tip: If the event is full you can join the waiting list: if a spot frees up, you get in automatically.
events.step3Text: Want to organise a meetup in your city or online? Tap “Organise an event”.
events.step4Text: To organise events you need to be a Verified Kumano: tap “Become a verified organiser” and follow the steps. Then, from “My events”, you manage attendees and check-in.

antitruffa.title: Anti-Scam Manual
antitruffa.summary: The most common scams, with real examples and what to do right away: read it, save it and share it with the people you love.
antitruffa.step1Text: At the top, tap “Download or print the manual”: your phone’s or computer’s print window opens, where you can also save it as a PDF.
antitruffa.step2Title: Share it with the people you love
antitruffa.step2Text: Send it to parents, grandparents and friends via WhatsApp, Facebook, Telegram, X, LinkedIn or email, or copy the link. Anyone who signs up from your link joins your network.
antitruffa.step3Text: Before clicking, replying or paying, ask yourself the 6 questions of the test: if even one answer is “yes”, it’s almost certainly a scam.
antitruffa.step3Tip: Right below are the 6 golden rules: they alone are enough to avoid most scams.
antitruffa.step4Text: From the contents, go to the chapter you need: email and texts, phone calls, at your front door, chats, shopping, investments… Tap a scam to open it and read examples and what to do. At the end you’ll find what to do right away if you’ve been scammed.

verifica_iban.title: IBAN Check
verifica_iban.summary: Check the IBAN before a bank transfer: whether it’s written correctly, which country it’s from and which warning signs to watch for.
verifica_iban.step1Text: Paste the IBAN you were given, with or without spaces, and tap “Check the IBAN”. The check happens entirely on your phone: the IBAN is never sent or saved.
verifica_iban.step2Text: You see whether the IBAN is written correctly and which country it’s from. For Italian IBANs you also see its parts: CIN, ABI (the bank), CAB (the branch) and account number.
verifica_iban.step2Tip: If there’s a mistake, we tell you where: for example a missing character or two swapped digits.
verifica_iban.step3Text: Choose the closest answer (a private seller, a holiday home, an online shop, an investment…) and your country: we show you the warning signs to watch for.
verifica_iban.step4Text: Remember: a valid IBAN doesn’t guarantee the recipient is honest. Read the tips before paying: an instant transfer can’t be cancelled.

checkmail.title: CheckMail
checkmail.summary: Got a suspicious email? Upload or copy it: we check the sender, links, attachments and text and tell you how risky it is.
checkmail.step1Title: Choose how to load the email
checkmail.step1Text: There are three ways: “Upload the file” (the email saved as .eml or .msg, the most complete), “Paste the source” or “From your phone”. Each one comes with instructions for Gmail, Outlook and other programs.
checkmail.step2Title: Enter the email and analyse it
checkmail.step2Text: From your phone, just copy the sender, subject and text with any links, then tap “Analyze the email”.
checkmail.step2Tip: Below the button you can see how many checks you have left today.
checkmail.step3Text: The result tells you whether the risk is low, medium or high and lists what we found: fake sender, shortened links, pressure, requests for your details…
checkmail.step4Text: Follow the advice: for example don’t click, don’t open attachments and don’t reply. With “Check another email” you start again.
checkmail.step4Tip: CheckMail gives clues, not certainties: if in doubt, contact the company through its official channels.

verifoto.title: VeriFoto
verifoto.summary: Check whether a photo is real or was created or retouched with artificial intelligence, before you trust it.
verifoto.step1Text: Tap “Choose a photo” and pick the image to check (JPG, PNG or WebP up to 15 MB). The basic checks happen on your phone.
verifoto.step2Title: The risk that it’s AI or retouched
verifoto.step2Text: You see a verdict and a risk percentage: 0–30% low, 31–69% uncertain, 70–100% high. Below are the clues found, such as digital certificates and camera data.
verifoto.step3Text: Tap “Retouch map”: areas much brighter than the rest can point to pasted or retouched parts. It’s a visual aid, not proof.
verifoto.step4Title: Second opinion and the original photo
verifoto.step4Text: For an extra check use the AI detector: agree to send a reduced copy of the photo and tap “Analyse with the AI detector”. With Google Lens or TinEye you can search whether the same photo already exists online.
verifoto.step4Tip: VeriFoto gives clues, not certainties: if in doubt, don’t trust it.

documento_sicuro.title: Safe Document
documento_sicuro.summary: Before sending a photo of an ID, add a caption with purpose and date and cover the details that aren’t needed.
documento_sicuro.step1Title: Choose the photo of the document
documento_sicuro.step1Text: Tap “Choose a photo” to pick it from your gallery or “Take a photo”. The photo stays on your phone: it’s never uploaded or saved.
documento_sicuro.step2Title: Cover the details that aren’t needed
documento_sicuro.step2Text: Tap “Cover an area” and drag your finger over the photo to put a black rectangle over the document number, signature or photo, if they weren’t asked for.
documento_sicuro.step2Tip: We also tell you if the photo contains hidden data, such as GPS location: it’s gone from the downloaded copy.
documento_sicuro.step3Text: Choose what you’re sending it for (renting, bank, job, online purchase…) and to whom: the caption with purpose and date repeats diagonally across the whole photo. You can change its text, visibility, size and colour.
documento_sicuro.step3Tip: Use a different caption for each person: if the copy gets passed around, you’ll know where it came from.
documento_sicuro.step4Text: Tap “Download the protected copy” or “Share”: you get a new copy with the caption and covered areas, without hidden data. The original isn’t touched.

listings.title: Community Listings
listings.summary: Post services and products, find what you need and message whoever posted.
listings.step1Text: Type what you’re looking for, choose category, country and city and tap “Search”. Featured listings appear first.
listings.step2Text: Tap “New Listing”: posting costs some KU Karma, shown on the button. Write a title, category and description; price and image are optional.
listings.step2Tip: If you don’t have enough KU Karma, log in every day to collect them. Listings last 30 days, then you can repost them with one click.
listings.step3Text: Choose country and city. For services and consulting, tick “Also available online / remotely”: the listing appears in every city of the country.
listings.step4Text: You can feature the listing right away in the Featured section with KU Points, choosing for how many days. Then tap “Publish Listing”.
listings.step5Text: In “My messages” you’ll find conversations with people who wrote to you about a listing or whom you wrote to. For your privacy, messages are deleted automatically after 30 days.

timebank.title: KUMANI Time Bank
timebank.summary: Help someone for an hour and earn an hour, to spend when you need a hand.
timebank.step1Text: You help someone for an hour and earn an hour, which you spend when you need a hand. Hours aren’t worth money and can’t be turned into points or discounts.
timebank.step2Text: Tap “Verify and join”: you need to have been a member for at least 30 days, a complete profile, be of age, a verified identity (tax code or ID) and accepted rules. Then you create your profile and get your welcome hours.
timebank.step2Tip: You can verify your identity and accept the rules right away, even if some requirement is still missing.
timebank.step3Text: On the board, filter requests and offers by category, in person or online, and city. Post with “Ask for help” or “Offer help”, or reply with “I can help”: hours move from one balance to the other when you both confirm.
timebank.step4Text: The first time, meet in a public place or online. Nobody should ask you for money, gifts or bank details; no professional advice or dangerous jobs. If something’s wrong, report it: the Staff steps in.

convivio.title: Kordata
convivio.summary: Group buying among Kumani: together you buy better, straight from the producer or the shop.
convivio.step1Text: A Kumano proposes a group purchase from a producer or shop and the others join: once the minimum is reached the order goes ahead and everyone pays the supplier directly.
convivio.step2Text: Under “Open” you’ll find active Kordate, by category (food and wine, tech, travel and events, home and energy…). Open the one you like and tap “I’m in”: we’ll let you know when the minimum is reached. Under “Mine” you’ll find the ones you’re part of.
convivio.step2Tip: Once you join you can see who’s taking part and write in the group chat.
convivio.step3Text: Tap “Propose a Kordata”. To protect those who join you need to become an organiser: an active subscription for at least 30 days, a complete profile, a verified identity and the organiser’s rules accepted.
convivio.step4Text: KUMANI doesn’t handle payments: once the minimum is reached, everyone pays the supplier directly following the organiser’s instructions, and the organiser is responsible for what they propose.

affinity.title: KUMANI Affinity
affinity.summary: A 20-question game to discover your archetype, challenge a friend and meet people on your wavelength.
affinity.step1Text: Tap “Start the game” and answer 20 quick questions: there are no right or wrong answers.
affinity.step1Tip: We only save your map (5 values) and your archetype, never your individual answers. You can delete it whenever you like.
affinity.step2Text: At the end you discover your KUMANI archetype and your Affinity Map on 5 values: adventure, values, rhythm, curiosity and warmth. You can share it or play again.
affinity.step3Text: Tap “Send the Duo link” and send it to a friend or partner: they play, even without signing up, and you instantly find out how compatible you are.
affinity.step4Text: Every week Kumi introduces you to a few people on your wavelength. Choose the languages you speak, add a sentence about yourself, give your consent and tap “Turn on introductions”. The chat only opens if you both say yes.
affinity.step4Tip: Only subscribed adults who chose to take part are included. You can block, report or pause whenever you like.

veritas.title: Veritas
veritas.summary: The “Who’s lying?” game for 3 to 8 players: friends can play even without signing up.
veritas.step1Text: Enter your nickname, choose the question language and number of rounds and tap “Create the room”. Invite friends with the link or code: 3 to 8 players, even without signing up.
veritas.step2Text: If a friend has already created a room, enter their code and tap “Join the room”.
veritas.step3Text: Each round brings a question: everyone writes the truth, except one person who secretly makes something up. Read the anonymous answers and vote for the liar. Whoever spots the liar gets 1 point; the liar gets 1 point for each person fooled.

kumani_cv.title: KUMANI CV
