nfcTag.buyText: An NFC tag of type NTAG213, NTAG215 or NTAG216: sticker, card or key ring. They cost a few cents each online and any of these types will do.
nfcTag.buyMetal: If you stick it on the back of a phone with a magnetic (MagSafe) case or on a metal surface, choose an “anti-metal” tag: normal ones don’t work there.
nfcTag.linkLabel: The link to write on the tag
nfcTag.androidStep1: Make sure NFC is on: Settings → Connected devices (or Connections) → NFC.
nfcTag.androidStep3: Tap “Write to tag” and, the first time, allow KUMANI to use NFC.
nfcTag.androidStep4: Hold the tag against the middle of the back of the phone until “Done” appears.
nfcTag.waiting: Hold the tag near the phone…
nfcTag.done: Done! The link is on the tag. Try it with another phone.
nfcTag.denied: NFC permission denied. Allow it in Chrome’s site settings (padlock next to the address → Permissions) and try again.
nfcTag.error: Writing failed. Check that NFC is on, bring the tag close again and hold it still for a couple of seconds.
nfcTag.androidNoChrome: This browser can’t write NFC tags from a website. On Android open this page in Chrome, or use the free NFC Tools app as explained for iPhone.
nfcTag.androidAlt: You can also use the free NFC Tools app (Google Play) on Android, with the same steps as for iPhone.
nfcTag.iphoneIntro: On iPhone websites can’t write NFC tags (Apple doesn’t allow it in Safari): use the free NFC Tools app, it takes a minute.
nfcTag.iphoneStep1: Download NFC Tools for free from the App Store.
nfcTag.iphoneStep3: In NFC Tools open “Write” → “Add a record” → “URL / URI”.
nfcTag.iphoneStep4: Paste the link in the field (nothing else) and confirm with “OK”.
nfcTag.iphoneStep5: Tap “Write” and, when “Ready to scan” appears, hold the tag near the top of the back of the iPhone.
nfcTag.iphoneModels: Writing requires an iPhone 7 or later.
nfcTag.readIphone: iPhone XS and later: with the screen on, hold the top of the back near the tag and tap the notification that appears.
nfcTag.readIphoneOld: iPhone 7, 8 and X: open Control Center and tap “NFC Tag Reader” (add it in Settings → Control Center).
nfcTag.readAndroid: Android: with NFC on and the screen unlocked, hold the middle of the back near the tag: the page opens by itself.
nfcTag.tipTest: After writing it, test it with another phone, or close Chrome first: if the page that wrote the tag is still open, the link may stop in the address bar.
nfcTag.tipLock: In NFC Tools you can “lock” the tag so nobody can change it, but it’s permanent: you won’t be able to rewrite it. Lock it only once you’ve checked it works.

card.title: NFC business card
card.intro: Write your card link on an NFC sticker or card: anyone who taps it with their phone opens your business card, on iPhone and Android, with no app to install.
card.linkHint: It’s the same link as the QR code: it opens your card page with the contacts you chose to show.
card.readTitle: How it’s read (for whoever receives the card)
card.tipUpdate: If you change the contacts shown or the card design, you don’t need to rewrite the tag: the link stays the same.
card.tipQr: Keep the QR code on the paper card too: people whose phone has no NFC can scan it with the camera.

review.title: NFC sticker for reviews
review.intro: Write your review link on an NFC sticker: customers tap it with their phone and the page to leave you a review opens straight away, on iPhone and Android, with no app.
review.linkHint: It’s the review link entered above: the tag holds the direct link, so it opens immediately.
review.tipUpdate: If you change the review link, rewrite the sticker: the link is stored inside the tag.
review.tipQr: Put a QR code with the same link next to the sticker too: people whose phone has no NFC can scan it with the camera.
review.placeText: Near the till, on the counter, on tables or in the window, with clearly visible text, for example: “Enjoyed it? Tap your phone here and leave us a review”. Counter stands with the tag already inside are also available.
review.noLink: Enter the review link above (for example your Google one) and save: then you can write it on an NFC sticker.

vocaleSospetto.heroTitle: Does a voice message seem odd?
vocaleSospetto.heroText: “Hi mum, I’ve changed my number”, the fake police officer, the fake bank asking for a code: let KUMANI listen and see if it has the typical signs of a scam.
vocaleSospetto.howTitle: How do you want to check it?
vocaleSospetto.optFileHint: From WhatsApp: press and hold the message → Forward/Share → Save to Files, then choose it here.
vocaleSospetto.optRecordHint: Play the message out loud (even from another phone) and tap here. Up to 3 minutes.
vocaleSospetto.optTextHint: If WhatsApp already showed you the transcript, copy and paste it.
vocaleSospetto.textPlaceholder: Paste the text of the voice message here
vocaleSospetto.downloadNote: Only the first time, voice recognition is downloaded (about 80 MB, better on Wi-Fi). Then it stays on your phone.
vocaleSospetto.errorLong: The message is too long: 3 minutes at most.
vocaleSospetto.errorAudio: This phone can’t read the file. Try “Let the microphone listen”.
vocaleSospetto.errorNoVoice: I didn’t hear any words. Try again closer to the speaker.
vocaleSospetto.errorModel: Voice recognition didn’t start. Try again, better on Wi-Fi.
vocaleSospetto.errorMic: I can’t use the microphone: allow it in your browser settings.
vocaleSospetto.risk_high: Careful: this really looks like a scam
vocaleSospetto.riskText_high: The message has several typical scam signs together. Don’t send money or codes, and check by calling the person yourself on the number you know.
vocaleSospetto.riskText_medium: Some phrases sound like scammers’ ones. Before doing anything, check calmly.
vocaleSospetto.riskText_low: One sign alone isn’t enough to call it a scam, but it’s worth checking.
vocaleSospetto.riskText_none: We found no typical scam phrases. Still be careful if they ask for money or data.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_family: The classic “hi mum, I’ve changed my number”: scammers pretend to be a child or relative.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_accident: Accident, hospital, arrest, bail: meant to scare you into paying fast.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_money: Transfers, top-ups, gift cards or crypto: people who love you don’t ask for them in a voice message.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_iban: They dictate an IBAN or account: check it with IBAN Check before paying.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_code: No bank, post office or serious person asks you to read out a code you got by text.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_remote: AnyDesk, TeamViewer or “remote assistance” are used to take control of your phone.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_urgency: “Now”, “by today”, “otherwise…”: hurry is meant to stop you thinking.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_secrecy: “Don’t tell anyone”: scammers don’t want you to ask for advice.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_authority: Police, lawyers, tax office: real authorities don’t ask for money on the phone.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_bank: “Account blocked”, “unusual access”: hang up and call your bank on its official number.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_courier: Shipping or storage fees to pay through a link: a very common scam.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_investment: No serious investment guarantees earnings or doubles them.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_prize: If you didn’t enter any contest, you can’t have won.
vocaleSospetto.sigText_link: Don’t open links from strangers: check them first with Speculum.
vocaleSospetto.advice1: Don’t send money, codes or photos of documents.
vocaleSospetto.advice2: Call the person or organisation yourself on the number you know, not the one in the message.
vocaleSospetto.advice3: Talk to someone you trust before deciding.
vocaleSospetto.advice4: If it’s a scam, report the number: you protect others too.
vocaleSospetto.report: Report the number to the Anti-Scam Network
vocaleSospetto.privacy: The message is listened to and transcribed on your phone: we don’t upload it and nobody listens to it. The check recognises typical scam signs in Italian; it can’t tell whether a voice is real or AI-generated.
vocaleSospetto.italianOnly: The check recognises scam phrases in Italian only: with messages in other languages it may miss the warning signs.

fonometro.heroTitle: How much noise is there really?
fonometro.heroText: Noisy neighbours, a bar downstairs, building work: measure the decibels, keep a log of the loudest moments and download a PDF with chart and times.
fonometro.errorMic: I can’t use the microphone: allow it in your browser settings.
fonometro.errorSave: Phone storage is full: delete some measurements from the log.
fonometro.errorPdf: The PDF wasn’t created. Try again.
fonometro.level_danger: Extremely loud: harmful to ears over time
fonometro.liveLine: {time} · average {average} dB · max {max} dB · {events, plural, one {# moment} other {# moments}} above the threshold
fonometro.keepOn: Keep the screen on and the phone still, with the microphone uncovered.
fonometro.thresholdHint: Above this threshold KUMANI notes the time and length of the noise. At night at home 40–45 dB is already annoying.
fonometro.calibrationHint: Every phone hears differently. If you have a real sound meter or a calibrated app, measure the same noise and adjust until the numbers match.
fonometro.logLine: average {average} dB · max {max} dB · {events, plural, one {# moment} other {# moments}}
fonometro.disclaimer: A phone microphone isn’t a calibrated instrument: values are an estimate, useful for comparing times and places, not a legally valid measurement. No audio is recorded: only the volume is measured, and everything stays on your phone.
fonometro.discardConfirm: Discard this measurement? If you saved it, it’s removed from the log too.

metronomo.heroText: A metronome with sound and light that, if you like, listens to your hits and tells you if you’re early, late or spot on.
metronomo.liveLine: {hits, plural, one {# hit} other {# hits}} · {percent}% in time
metronomo.errorMic: I can’t use the microphone: the metronome plays, but without listening.
metronomo.accelHint: +{step} beats every {bars, plural, one {bar} other {# bars}}, up to {target}.
metronomo.listenHint: The microphone hears your hits (drums, guitar, piano, hands) and compares them with the beats.
metronomo.headphones: For accurate listening use headphones, or choose “Light only”: that way the microphone doesn’t hear the metronome click.
metronomo.resultHits: {hits} hits, {onTime} in time, at {bpm} beats per minute.
metronomo.tendencyNone: Neither early nor late: great balance!
metronomo.tendencyEarly: On average you’re {ms} ms early: relax and wait for the beat.
metronomo.tendencyLate: On average you’re {ms} ms late: play the hit a little sooner.
metronomo.chartHint: Each dot is a hit: on the line in time, below early, above late.
metronomo.privacy: No sound is recorded: only the hits are listened to, and everything stays on your phone. It works best with percussive sounds (drums, guitar, piano, hands) rather than sustained ones (violin, flute, voice).

metronomo.keysHint: Keyboard: space starts and stops, arrows change the tempo (with Shift by 5).

accordatore.heroTitle: Your instrument in tune in no time
accordatore.heroText: Guitar, bass, ukulele, violin, viola and cello, alternate tunings too: play a string and the needle tells you if it’s right, to the cent.
accordatore.errorMic: I can’t use the microphone: allow it in your browser settings.
accordatore.flatHint: Tighten the string a little (turn the peg to raise the note).
accordatore.sharpHint: Loosen the string a little (turn the peg to lower the note).
accordatore.autoHint: I detect the string by myself. Tap one to tune only that string and hear its note.
accordatore.manualHint: Tuning only {note}. Tap it again to go back to automatic detection.
accordatore.a4Hint: Usually 440 Hz. Orchestras and choirs often use 442; early music 415.
accordatore.strobe: Strobe mode (maximum precision: the stripes stop when it’s in tune)
accordatore.sensitivityHint: Raise it in a quiet room or for soft-sounding instruments; lower it if there’s noise around.
accordatore.privacy: No sound is recorded: the note is detected on your phone and nothing leaves the device.
accordatore.guided: Step by step, one string at a time
accordatore.guidedHint: Follow the guide below: tap a string to choose it yourself.
accordatore.guideDrawing: Drawing of the instrument with the peg to turn
accordatore.guidePlay: Play this string on its own.
accordatore.guideRaise: Turn the peg the way the arrow shows: the note goes up.
accordatore.guideLower: Turn the peg the way the arrow shows: the note goes down.
accordatore.guideLeftHint: Pegs on the left: anticlockwise tightens the string and raises the note.
accordatore.guideRightHint: Pegs on the right: clockwise tightens the string and raises the note.
accordatore.guideBowedHint: Use the fine tuner on the tailpiece: clockwise raises the note. If it’s far off, gently turn the peg at the top, pushing it in.

registroOre.title: Hours and shifts log
registroOre.heroText: Log your shifts with one tap and check your payslip at the end of the month: regular hours, overtime, Sundays and holidays.
registroOre.firstPlaceText: Write the name of your workplace. If you work in more than one place, you can add them later.
registroOre.hourlyRateHint: You can find it in your contract or payslip. It is only used for an estimate.
registroOre.thresholdsHint: Hours above these count as overtime. Usually 8 a day and 40 a week: check your contract.
registroOre.deletePlaceConfirm: Delete “{name}”? All its shifts will be deleted too.
registroOre.startShiftHint: Records the start now. You can correct the time later.
registroOre.startTimeHint: The current time is already filled in. Change it if you started earlier.
registroOre.startedNotice: Shift started at {time}. Have a good day!
registroOre.openTooLong: This shift has been open for many hours: did you forget to end it? Tap “End shift” and enter the right time.
registroOre.repeatConfirm: You already have shifts today. Do you want to add yesterday’s as well?
registroOre.repeatedNotice: {n, plural, one {Copied # shift from yesterday to today.} other {Copied # shifts from yesterday to today.}}
registroOre.overnightHint: If you finish after midnight, write the time as it is (e.g. 18:00 – 02:00): the shift counts on the day it started.
registroOre.markHolidayHint: For holidays that are not national, such as the local patron saint. National holidays are recognised automatically.
registroOre.markNightHint: All hours of this shift count as night hours.
registroOre.previewNextDay: The shift ends the next day.
registroOre.grossNote: This is an estimate to check your payslip, not a payslip calculation: hours times hourly pay, without extra rates, contributions or taxes.
registroOre.grossPartial: Hours at workplaces without an hourly pay are not included.
registroOre.noRateHint: Enter the hourly pay in the workplace to also see a gross pay estimate.
registroOre.calendarHint: Tap a day to see or add shifts. Sundays and holidays are in red.
registroOre.weeksHint: Hours of each week (Monday to Sunday) compared with the regular hours per week.
registroOre.weekCrossesMonth: Week spanning two months: it also counts the days of the other month.
registroOre.pdfNameLabel: Your name (shown at the top of the PDF)
registroOre.pdfError: I couldn’t create the PDF. Please try again.
registroOre.how1: Hours worked = from the start to the end of the shift, minus the break. On the nights when the clocks change, the real time counts.
registroOre.how2: Overtime = hours above the regular hours per day, day by day. Below you also see the comparison with the regular hours per week.
registroOre.how3: A shift that goes past midnight counts on the day it started; for Sundays and holidays the hours after midnight count on the right day.
registroOre.how4: Italian national holidays (New Year, Epiphany, Easter and Easter Monday, 25 April, 1 May, 2 June, 15 August, All Saints, 8, 25 and 26 December) are recognised automatically. Mark the local patron saint with “Public holiday”.
registroOre.how5: Your contract may count differently: these numbers help you check your payslip and talk about it with whoever prepares it.

ricevutaOccasionale.title: Occasional work receipt
ricevutaOccasionale.heroTitle: The right receipt, without a VAT number
ricevutaOccasionale.heroText: For people who work now and then. Enter your fee: we work out the withholding tax, the revenue stamp and the net amount. Then download the PDF to sign.
ricevutaOccasionale.disclaimer: This is a helper tool: it does the maths with the most common rules. For special cases, ask an accountant or a CAF (tax assistance centre).
ricevutaOccasionale.profileFirstText: Name, tax code and address go on every receipt. You only enter them once.
ricevutaOccasionale.profileIntro: These are the details of the person issuing the receipt: you. We save them for your next receipts.
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldTaxCodeHint: 16 characters, as on your health card.
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldIbanHint: If you enter it, it appears on the receipt for the bank transfer.
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldDefaultPlaceHint: The town shown next to the date, before the signature.
ricevutaOccasionale.profileSavedFirst: Details saved. Now you can make your first receipt.
ricevutaOccasionale.kindPrivateText: A private person (for themselves or their family), someone with a VAT number under the flat-rate scheme (forfettario), or someone abroad.
ricevutaOccasionale.kindWithholdingText: A company, a professional under the ordinary regime, an organisation or a condominium: they keep 20% and pay it to the State for you. If in doubt, ask the client whether they apply withholding tax.
ricevutaOccasionale.emptyClients: No saved clients yet. You can add them here or while making a receipt.
ricevutaOccasionale.clientsHint: If you delete a client, receipts already made do not change.
ricevutaOccasionale.deleteClientConfirm: Delete the client “{name}”? Their receipts stay.
ricevutaOccasionale.rememberClient: Save this client for future receipts
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldIssueDateLockedHint: The number belongs to {year}: the date must stay in that year.
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldDescriptionPlaceholder: For example: translation of a document from English into Italian
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldGrossHint: The amount agreed, before withholding tax.
ricevutaOccasionale.amountInvalid: Enter a valid amount, for example 150 or 150.50.
ricevutaOccasionale.expensesWarning: Usually refunds are added to the fee and withholding tax is also calculated on them. If in doubt, leave it like this.
ricevutaOccasionale.expensesOnBehalf: These are costs paid in the client’s name and on their behalf, with receipts or invoices in their name: leave them out of the withholding tax.
ricevutaOccasionale.calcNoWithholding: No withholding: the client is not a withholding agent.
ricevutaOccasionale.calcChooseClient: Choose the client to see if withholding tax applies.
ricevutaOccasionale.stampRequired: The amount is over €77.47: the original needs a €2 revenue stamp. Who pays for it?
ricevutaOccasionale.stampChargeClient: The client: €2 is added to the total
ricevutaOccasionale.stampChargeIssuer: Me: the total does not change
ricevutaOccasionale.fieldStampIdHint: The digits printed on the stamp. You can add it after buying it.
ricevutaOccasionale.stampNotRequired: Up to €77.47 no revenue stamp is needed.
ricevutaOccasionale.inpsOverInForm: With this receipt your {year} fees reach {total}: above €5,000 you must register with the INPS Gestione Separata for the part above.
ricevutaOccasionale.inpsOver: In {year} you went {over} over €5,000 of occasional work fees: for the part above you must register with the INPS Gestione Separata. Ask an accountant or a CAF.
ricevutaOccasionale.inpsNear: You are {left} away from €5,000 of fees this year: above that amount you must register with the INPS Gestione Separata.
ricevutaOccasionale.inpsHint: The €5,000 limit counts all your occasional work fees for the year, including those not recorded here. Cancelled receipts do not count.
ricevutaOccasionale.unpaidConfirm: Mark receipt no. {number}/{year} as not paid?
ricevutaOccasionale.cancelConfirm: Cancel receipt no. {number}/{year}? It stays in the list with its number, but does not count in the totals.
ricevutaOccasionale.deleteConfirm: Delete receipt no. {number}/{year}? This cannot be undone.
ricevutaOccasionale.deleteHint: Only the last receipt of the year can be deleted, so the numbers stay in order. The others can be cancelled.
ricevutaOccasionale.markPaidText: Has {client} paid you {net}? Enter the payment date.
ricevutaOccasionale.receiptCreated: Receipt no. {number}/{year} created. Download the PDF, sign it and hand it over.
ricevutaOccasionale.pdfError: We could not create the PDF. Please try again.
